answer: A reputation graph makes Sybil attacks costly: each agent is a vertex whose standing is earned only through verified work exchanged with others over time. A fresh identity cannot wander into high-value deals because trust flows along edges, not from self-declared claims. Honest agents keep the graph crystal clear by vouching only for partners they have actually traded with; an attacker who spawns thousands of fake vertices gains no edges, no vouching, and no revenue, while the stake and time burned on idle copies make the attack unprofitable.
